assertions.description: Navigator exposes a playHaptics member (the imperative semantic-haptics entry point).
navigator.playHaptics is a function, per the proposed partial Navigator interface.
Calling playHaptics with a valid effect returns undefined — the API exposes no success signal, even when the call is silently ignored for lack of activation.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof navigator.playHaptics !== 'function') return false; return navigator.playHaptics('tick') === undefined; })()

assertions.description: HapticEffect is a closed enum (hint, edge, tick, align in the Chromium IDL), so an unknown effect name is rejected with a TypeError by the WebIDL binding.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof navigator.playHaptics !== 'function') return false; try { navigator.playHaptics('not-a-real-effect'); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: intensity is a WebIDL double (not unrestricted), so NaN is rejected with a TypeError at the binding before any clamping.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof navigator.playHaptics !== 'function') return false; try { navigator.playHaptics('tick', NaN); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: A finite out-of-range intensity (e.g. 2.5) is accepted by the binding and clamped to [0,1] internally — the call still returns undefined rather than throwing.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof navigator.playHaptics !== 'function') return false; try { return navigator.playHaptics('tick', 2.5) === undefined; } catch (e) { return false; } })()

assertions.description: playHaptics declares exactly one required argument (effect); intensity is optional with default 1.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof navigator.playHaptics !== 'function') return false; return navigator.playHaptics.length === 1; })()

assertions.description: A policy-controlled feature named 'haptics' is registered (it ships together with the WebHaptics flag via depends_on), observable through permissions-policy introspection.
assertions.test: (() => { const fp = document.featurePolicy || document.permissionsPolicy; if (!fp || typeof fp.features !== 'function') return false; return fp.features().includes('haptics'); })()

assertions.description: Physically feeling an effect requires a haptics-capable most-recent input device (first backend: Windows 11 24H2+ touchpad/mouse/pen), and the API deliberately exposes no signal of whether output played — so actual output cannot be asserted from script.
assertions.test: Requires haptic hardware and OS support; the API's anti-fingerprinting design makes success unobservable to the page.
